title: Faster delivery: stacked dispatch of dependent tasks, sync of dependency fixes and a test-selection pre-flight
goal: Let a dependent task start from its in-flight dependency's branch while that dependency is still verified, keep unverified code out through a gate, tell the dependent's lead when the dependency moved, and make an expensive test selection visible before it runs.

tasks.objective: Stacked dispatch, part 1: base, record and status. start_base (factory-pipeline.py ~1258) returns the dependency's branch tip when exactly one dependency is candidate or reviewed and every other dependency is integrated; with two in-flight dependencies the task keeps waiting. A state file <task>__stack.json records {dep, dep branch, dep sha, at} by SHA, never by branch name, outside task_fingerprint. own_start (~3558) and review_base (~3449) use the newest dependency SHA contained in HEAD (its PASS SHA preferred) so --affected --base sees only the dependent's own delta. status shows 'stacked on D@X' and, when D moved, 'D now at Y not in HEAD' with the merge command as next. A no-worktree repo and tier XS never stack. Tests use the throwaway-repo harness of tests/pipeline.test.sh and the in-process cases of multiwave.py.
acceptance: a dependent of one candidate dependency is stackable and its spec base is the dependency tip; with two in-flight dependencies it is not
the stack record holds SHAs only and does not change the task fingerprint (existing verdicts stay valid)
own_start and review_base of a stacked task exclude the dependency's commits, proven by the --affected --base value dispatch prints
status prints the stacked and moved notes with the merge command as next
existing multiwave and base cases pass unchanged

tasks.objective: Stacked dispatch, part 2: the rules that keep unverified code out. dispatch --phase verify|review|qa for a stacked task exits 2 until the dependency's PASS SHA is an ancestor of the task's HEAD; verdict refuses a PASS whose sha lacks it; gate blocks a dependent integrated before its dependency and any dependent without the dependency PASS SHA; a merge-from-dependency commit in the dependent is credited as a sync merge (only conflict resolutions count) in _uncovered_changes; integration order stays dependency first, then the dependent with git merge --no-ff.
acceptance: verify dispatch for a stacked task before the dependency PASS is merged in exits 2 with the reason
verdict PASS on a sha without the dependency PASS SHA is refused
gate lists a blocker for a dependent integrated first and for a missing dependency PASS SHA, and none after the correct order
a merge-from-dependency commit does not make the dependency's review STALE, a conflict resolution outside the owned paths does

tasks.objective: Stacked dispatch, part 3: tell the dependent when the dependency moved. New verb sync plan.json --task <D> [--send]: for each stacked dependent whose HEAD lacks D's latest candidate or PASS SHA it prints, and with --send runs, orca orchestration send --to run:<dependent lead run> --type status --subject 'sync: D moved to <sha>' --body '<one-line git merge command>' (@worktree:<id> as the fallback address), and writes a durable <task>__sync.json that status shows, because a message is only a nudge. lead_prompt tells the dependent's lead to run git merge <D branch> (never rebase) at each subtask boundary when status shows sync, resolve conflicts inside its owned paths, then continue. Tested with the fake orca of tests/pipeline.test.sh.
acceptance: sync prints the merge command and the fake orca receives one status message per stale dependent with --send
status shows the sync note until the dependent's HEAD contains the dependency SHA, then clears it
without Orca the verb prints the commands and exits 0; an unknown task is a usage error (exit 2)

tasks.objective: Stacked dispatch, part 4: the handoff and cleanup. dispatch --phase lead for a stackable task prints git worktree add --no-track -b <topic>-<id> <path> <dependency tip sha>, then orca worktree set with the integration checkout as parent (a sibling, never a branch named <dep branch>--*), then the launch, and a prompt that says: implement now, run no verify before status clears it. cleanup and status list stacked siblings with their dependency and the merge order (dependency first, then dependents, git branch -d only after the merge). A no-worktree repo never stacks.
acceptance: the printed worktree add uses the dependency tip and the topic-id branch name
the orca worktree set parent is the integration checkout
cleanup names the merge order and does not treat the stacked task as a child of its dependency
a task without a worktree repo or at tier XS prints the unchanged handoff

tasks.objective: Make a wide test selection visible before it costs an hour. dispatch --phase verify|qa prints 'selected N of M suites' (from affected.py, the count affected_case_lines already derives) and warns above a threshold (default 40) with the suggestion to narrow the paths or the checks. tests/run-all.sh writes per-suite durations to $STATE/run-all/timings.json (one line per suite) with no effect on pass or fail or on suite reuse, so a later step can estimate minutes. No new exit code. Also make run-all fail loudly when python3 cannot run: on this machine python3 in Git Bash is the Microsoft Store stub, tests/run-all.sh then silently falls back to 'no base, running everything' (seen in the finalize-verb verify: every suite ran), so it must print the reason and exit 2 for --affected instead of widening the run. A full run (no --affected) is unaffected.
acceptance: dispatch prints the selected and total suite counts and the warning above the threshold
run-all writes timings.json lines and its pass, fail and reuse behaviour is unchanged
no test depends on wall time
--affected with a python3 that cannot run exits 2 with the reason and runs no suite

tasks.objective: Write the rule and the skill text, once. skills/delivery/references/delivery.md (sections 4, 5, 7, 10 and the QA tiers note) gets a new <!-- policy:stacked-dispatch --> policy: a dependent task starts from its single in-flight dependency's tip as a sibling <topic>-<id> worktree, implements in parallel, never verifies before the dependency PASS SHA is in its tree, merges (never rebases) the dependency branch when told, and is integrated after the dependency. docs/pipeline-cli.md documents sync, the status notes and the gate rules. skills/factory-core/references/parallel-work.md gets the operating lessons with their reasons: any edit under scripts/assetgen/*.py selected every suite through the unsure leaf (fixed in affected-leaf-fix), scripts/factory-cmd.py widens the selection, a stacked verify waits for the dependency PASS, merge not rebase, one in-flight dependency, sibling not child worktree. skills/delivery/SKILL.md stays a pointer. Add the policy id and sentence to POLICY_IDS and POLICY_SENTENCE in tests/parallel-policy.test.sh.
acceptance: delivery.md holds the only copy of the policy and parallel-policy.test.sh passes with the new marker
pipeline-cli.md matches the implemented verbs, notes and refusals
skills-lint and the changelog check pass and no skill exceeds its line cap
tasks.grade_reason: policy and skill prose; behaviour is tested in the earlier tasks
